title: App Store Review Checklist for First-Time iOS Developers
subtitle: Avoid common rejection pitfalls and publish your first iOS application smoothly.
products: free ebook: Publish an iOS App Without a Mac
html:
Submitting your first iOS application to the App Store can feel intimidating, but the review process follows clear guidelines. Apple reviews thousands of apps daily, evaluating them for technical stability, user privacy, and design consistency.

By following a systematic preparation checklist before hitting submit, you can bypass the most frequent causes of rejection and significantly reduce your time to market.

Metadata and App Information

Your app store listing serves as the first impression for users and reviewers. Ensure your app name, subtitle, and keywords accurately represent the core functionality without making exaggerated claims or referencing competing platforms.

A common mistake is forgetting to include valid contact information and a functional support URL in App Store Connect. Reviewers must be able to reach you and test your support channels easily during the evaluation phase.

Account and Authentication Setup

If your application requires user registration or login, you must provide active demo credentials in the review notes. Reviewers cannot test features hidden behind paywalls or private user accounts without a designated testing profile.

Additionally, if your app integrates third-party login providers like Google or Apple, verify that these authentication flows work reliably on actual iOS devices before submission, as broken login buttons result in immediate rejection.

Privacy and Data Permissions

Apple places a high emphasis on user privacy and data transparency. Every time your application requests access to sensitive hardware such as the camera, microphone, or location services, you must supply a clear usage description in the Info.plist file.

Generic strings like "access needed" will be rejected by the review team. Write descriptive explanations that tell the user exactly why the app requires that specific permission to function correctly.

In-App Purchases and Subscriptions

Monetizing through digital goods requires strict adherence to Apple's payment guidelines. All digital content must use the official StoreKit framework, and you must link an active sandbox user account in the review notes so testers can verify the purchase flow.

Another frequent pitfall is omitting the mandatory restore purchases button for non-consumable items and subscriptions. Make sure this option is clearly visible in your app settings or paywall screen.

Performance and Stability Standards

Reviewers test applications across various device sizes and iOS versions to check for stability. Ensure your user interface scales correctly on both smaller iPhone screens and larger iPad displays without overlapping text or clipped buttons.

Remove any placeholder text, broken links, or unfinished features labeled as coming soon. Applications containing placeholder content are routinely flagged for incomplete implementation.

Preparing your app for review requires patience and attention to detail. Double-checking your privacy disclosures, providing functional demo accounts, and verifying payment flows will save you days of waiting.

Take time today to open App Store Connect, review your metadata, and complete a final dry run of your submission checklist before clicking the submit button.
